findings.issue_text: [BUG] The initializer includes I18n::Backend::Pluralization and Fallbacks into I18n::Backend::Simple, but in a Discourse production process the active I18n.backend is not guaranteed to be Simple — this diff's own translate_accelerator.rb patches the backend's load_locale/translate at the backend class level, and any non-Simple backend (e.g. a chained/custom backend installed elsewhere) never receives the Fallbacks module, so `I18n.backend.class.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)` may include into a class that is not the configured backend. In any deployment where I18n.backend is not an instance of I18n::Backend::Simple (or a subclass), fallbacks and pluralization are silently absent, translations missing from the current locale render as raw keys with no fallback to en, and the whole feature this PR ships is a no-op.

[ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList overrides Hash#[] but is assigned via `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new`; the i18n gem's Fallbacks backend reads fallbacks through its own instance state and (in i18n >= 1.1) exposes I18n.fallbacks as a read-only delegation to the backend, so this assignment works only if the vendored/patched i18n version defines a fallbacks= setter that this diff never shows. A future i18n gem upgrade that changes how fallbacks configuration is threaded through (fallbacks.config / backend state) breaks this initializer silently — SiteSetting-based fallback resolution stops being consulted and lookups fall back only to :en or nothing, hitting every translated request after the upgrade.

[ADVISORY] ensure_loaded! lazily initializes @loaded_locales only on its own call path, while the pre-existing translate() at line 68 dereferences @loaded_locales without initialization, so the invariant '@loaded_locales is non-nil' now depends on callers remembering to hit ensure_loaded!/translate first — and a backend class reload or a fresh process calling ensure_loaded!(x) before any translate still leaves `@loaded_locales.include?(config.locale)` in translate() safe only because ensure_loaded! happened to seed the array with one unrelated locale. The next change touching load_locale/translate can introduce a nil.include? NoMethodError on the first untranslated request in a fresh process; also loading a locale via ensure_loaded! does not mark it for the translate() fast path check, so the same locale can be loaded twice.

[BUG] ensure_loaded! is only called from ApplicationController#set_locale, so the fallback locales are never pre-loaded on any non-request rendering path (mailers, Sidekiq jobs, rake tasks, system messages). A background-rendered mailer or job that calls I18n.t with a user locale whose translations aren't yet loaded falls back through FallbackLocaleList to SiteSetting.default_locale/:en, and the Simple backend returns 'translation missing' strings to end users in emails and system messages, because nothing on those paths ever ran I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!.

[BUG] FallbackLocaleList#[] reads SiteSetting.default_locale on every I18n fallback resolution with no per-request caching beyond SiteSetting's own cache, and this Hash subclass discards all writes so any code that does I18n.fallbacks[locale] = [...] or I18n.fallbacks.defaults = ... silently no-ops. Plugins or core code (rails-i18n fallbacks API consumers) that mutate I18n.fallbacks via Hash writers get silently dropped settings, and every translation miss on a loaded-but-incomplete locale pays a SiteSetting lookup on the fallback resolution path.

[ADVISORY] The diff introduces a custom fallback chain and a new ensure_loaded! protocol (config/initializers/i18n.rb plus the TranslateAccelerator#ensure_loaded! implementation) with no test anywhere in the diff exercising them. A regression in the fallback order (e.g. SiteSetting.default_locale returned as a String vs the Symbol locale causing uniq to not dedupe, or ensure_loaded! failing to mark locales loaded) ships undetected; the next locale-related change has no safety net, and there is no spec asserting the documented 'user locale, site locale, english' order.

[ADVISORY] The file's first comment states 'order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb' but the initializer is named i18n.rb, and Rails loads config/initializers alphabetically, so nothing enforces that ordering constraint the file itself declares as required. If a future file lands in config/initializers that loads i18n.rb's dependencies or if freedom_patches is renamed, the stated load-order dependency is silently violated and the next refactorer gets a load-order boot failure with only a comment, not a filename, to explain it.

[ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but overrides #[] to unconditionally return a computed array, so any Hash semantics (stored mappings, #each/#keys/#merge/#dig) silently return nothing or the wrong thing, and any attempt by the I18n gem or app code to configure per-locale fallbacks via I18n.fallbacks[locale] = [...] is a silent no-op write. Any future caller (plugin or core code) that stores or enumerates fallback entries gets empty/no results with no error, and the override is invisible at the call site; developers debugging fallback behavior get bitten because the object looks like a mutable map but isn't.

[ADVISORY] The new ensure_loaded!(locale) duplicates the load-unless-loaded pattern that translate() at line 66 still hand-rolls inline, creating two parallel implementations of the same guard that will drift (ensure_loaded! initializes @loaded_locales with ||=; the inline check in translate does not). translate() crashes with NoMethodError on nil @loaded_locales on the first translation if any code path invokes translate before any load_locale call has run — but more concretely for scope: the next change to loading semantics must be made twice, and the two guards already diverge.

[ADVISORY] The PR titled 'Localization fallbacks' also moves the pluralization backend inclusion out of config/initializers/pluralization.rb and bundles it with the fallbacks initializer, an unrelated behavior-bearing config change traceable to no stated requirement, with the migration verified by nothing in the diff. If the initializer ordering assumption in the '# order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb' comment is wrong for any environment that loads initializers differently, pluralization and fallbacks silently load before the translate accelerator patch, and operators bisecting a pluralization regression in production will not think to look at a PR labeled 'fallbacks'.

[BUG] FallbackLocaleList#[] unconditionally computes its own list and ignores the Hash's stored contents, so the documented I18n fallbacks configuration API (I18n.fallbacks = {:de => [...]} or per-locale assignment I18n.fallbacks[locale] = [...]) is silently discarded — writes go into the Hash but every read bypasses them. Any plugin, engine, or ops code that sets explicit per-locale fallbacks (the standard way to express e.g. zh_TW -> zh_CN, which the TODO itself anticipates) stores a value that is never read; the custom fallback chain runs instead, and the misconfiguration produces wrong-language output with no error.

[BUG] Fallback resolution invokes SiteSetting.default_locale — a database-backed read — on every missing-translation lookup, including on threads where no DB connection is expected (boot-time initializers, migrations, background jobs before connection establishment, rescue paths after connection loss). I18n.t, which previously touched no storage, now hits SiteSetting (DB) whenever a key is missing in the current locale; during boot or in a job with no connection this raises (e.g. PG::ConnectionBad) inside translation lookup, converting a benign missing translation into a crash of that job/initializer, and it adds a synchronous DB read inside every translation miss on hot paths.

[ADVISORY] Moving fallback configuration from production-only environment files into a global initializer changes behavior in development and test: environments that previously surfaced 'translation missing' strings for incomplete locales now silently fall back to site-default/English text. Developers and the test suite no longer see missing-translation markers for partially-translated locales in dev/test — incomplete translations ship to production unnoticed because the environment that would have caught them was changed in the same diff that made production depend on fallbacks.

[ADVISORY] Preloading of fallback locales (I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!) is wired only into the ApplicationController#set_locale request path, so any non-request caller of I18n.t in a non-primary locale (scheduled jobs, mailers, message bus workers) performs fallback lookups against locales never preloaded by this path. Background jobs rendering user-locale content take the cold load_locale path (or, if the accelerator skips loading for locales it wasn't told about, get untranslated/missing output), and the per-request 'ensure loaded' guarantee the design depends on simply does not exist outside the controller lifecycle.

[ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList#[] evaluates SiteSetting.default_locale on every fallback-chain resolution, so every I18n lookup now depends on a live database connection. Any translation performed outside a request with DB access — asset precompilation, `rake db:create`/bootstrap steps, early-boot initializers, or any I18n.t call before the DB schema/settings table exists — raises a connection or missing-table error where the old `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` path used the plain I18n.default_locale config value; operators get a crashed precompile/boot task with no hint that localization fallbacks introduced the dependency.

[BUG] `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is invoked only from ApplicationController#set_locale, so fallback locales are loaded exclusively on web-request paths. Background jobs, ActionMailer deliveries, rake tasks, and Sidekiq/Scheduled jobs that set I18n.locale directly never trigger ensure_loaded!, so a translation missing in the job's locale falls back to an unloaded default_locale and emits the raw key / missing-translation exception into emails and queued work — exactly the artifacts the 'server-side localization fallbacks' intent promised to protect, silently uncovered outside the controller happy path.

[ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but its `[]` ignores all stored entries, so any assignment to I18n.fallbacks is a silent no-op read. Plugin authors or future core code following the standard i18n API (`I18n.fallbacks[:de] = [:de, :en]`, or passing a hash to configure per-locale chains) get the value silently discarded on the next lookup — the fallback chain always comes from the hardcoded [locale, site default, :en] rule — producing wrong-language output with no error raised at the point of misconfiguration.

[ADVISORY] The '# order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb' comment is documentation only — Rails loads initializers alphabetically and nothing enforces that i18n.rb runs after the freedom-patches that define the backend/TranslateAccelerator surface it calls (I18n.ensure_loaded!, the @loaded_locales state) — while the same commit renamed pluralization.rb into i18n.rb, moving it earlier in the alphabet from 'p' to 'i', demonstrating the ordering is luck of the filename. If a future initializer rename or a freedom-patch reordering lands, I18n.ensure_loaded! in the controller's before_action raises NoMethodError on every request (500s site-wide), and since the dependency is expressed only in a comment, nothing in CI or boot catches it.

[ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList#[] mixes the raw locale object with symbols and dedupes with .uniq, so when I18n.locale is a String (any code path that assigns a string locale rather than a symbol) the list contains both "pt" and :pt and the "user locale" entry fails to collapse with the symbol-keyed entries the backend stores translations under. Users on such locales get duplicate backend loads and lookups that miss the string-form key, surfacing fallback (English) text or missing-translation spans for strings that are actually translated; debugging is misdirected because the translation exists.

[ADVISORY] ensure_loaded! (and the pre-existing translate path) does an unsynchronized read-then-act on @loaded_locales, so on a multi-threaded server the first concurrent requests for a new locale both observe it absent and both call load_locale, double-parsing and double-writing the locale's translation files into the shared cache. Under a burst of cold-start requests on Puma/Unicorn threaded mode, translation files for the same locale are loaded twice; the work is wasted and the duplicated @loaded_locales entries mean subsequent include? checks are consistent, but a mid-load reader can observe a partially-populated translations hash for that locale.

[ADVISORY] set_locale now calls I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! on every request, which synchronously dereferences SiteSetting.default_locale inside the FallbackLocaleList#[] lookup, coupling a per-request before_action to a fresh fallback-list computation each time with no memoization of the computed list per locale. Every request in every controller pays a SiteSetting read plus Hash-subclass allocation and array build for a value that only changes when an admin edits default_locale; under fallback-enabled lookups this is a hot-path allocation regression, and any exception raised while computing the list during request handling surfaces as a 500 from a controller that previously only set a variable.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not include Fallbacks into `I18n::Backend::Simple`; it explicitly does `I18n.backend.class.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)`, which targets whatever backend class is configured at initializer time (and can be non-Simple, e.g. a chain). The claim that non-Simple backends “never receive the Fallbacks module” is not supported by the shown code. The pluralization include remains specifically on `I18n::Backend::Simple`, but that matches prior behavior (the deleted `pluralization.rb` did the same), so the finding’s described regression/no-op behavior isn’t verifiable from this diff alone.

The claim that this will definitely break on i18n >= 1.1 cannot be verified from the diff (no i18n version/backend API shown), but the general compatibility/upgrade fragility concern is grounded in the new initializer’s approach rather than being a concrete defect demonstrated by the PR.

adjudication.rationale: The finding hinges on @loaded_locales being nil in translate() and on ensure_loaded! not recording loaded locales for the translate() fast-path. But translate() already dereferenced @loaded_locales before this diff, so any nil.include? risk would have pre-existed unless @loaded_locales is initialized elsewhere in the file (not shown in the diff). Also the new ensure_loaded!(locale) initializes @loaded_locales ||= [] and then calls load_locale locale unless already included, so it does not inherently leave translate() with a nil @loaded_locales, nor does it inherently cause double-loading unless load_locale itself fails to mark locales (not verifiable from the diff).

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces explicit preloading of fallback locales via `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` and wires it only in `ApplicationController#set_locale` (`I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`). No other call sites are shown in the diff, so non-controller execution paths (e.g., mailers/jobs/rake) will not run this preloading step. Given the new `TranslateAccelerator#ensure_loaded!(locale)` and the fact `translate` only ensures `config.locale` is loaded, fallback locales may remain unloaded unless `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is invoked, potentially leading to missing translations when fallbacks are needed outside web requests.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces Rails’ standard fallbacks with a custom `FallbackLocaleList < Hash` where `#[]` ignores any stored hash entries and always recomputes `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]` (config/initializers/i18n.rb). That means any code that mutates the fallbacks via hash writers (e.g., `I18n.fallbacks[locale] = ...`) would not affect reads, which is a real compatibility/architecture concern introduced by this change. Also, `#[]` calls `SiteSetting.default_locale` every time it is invoked, which could add overhead on fallback resolution paths. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove core/plugins actually rely on mutating `I18n.fallbacks` or that this causes a correctness failure, so it’s better classified as a non-bug but important issue.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a custom fallback list where `FallbackLocaleList#[]` calls `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` (config/initializers/i18n.rb). That method is part of `I18n.fallbacks` and will be invoked during fallback resolution (i.e., when a translation is missing and fallbacks are consulted). This creates a runtime dependency on `SiteSetting` inside I18n lookup paths, whereas previously fallbacks were enabled via static `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` (now removed from multiple environment configs). If `SiteSetting.default_locale` requires DB access (as is typical for settings), translation misses (and also `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` now called in ApplicationController#set_locale) can trigger DB reads and potentially raise when no connection is available, turning a missing translation into an exception.

That’s a real, diff-grounded behavior/scope change affecting dev/test feedback, but it’s not provably a functional defect without project intent.

Background jobs rendering user-locale content take the cold load_locale path (or, if the accelerator skips loading for locales it wasn't told about, get untranslated/missing output), and the per-request 'ensure loaded' guarantee the design depends on simply does not exist outside the controller lifecycle.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` only in `ApplicationController#set_locale` (request lifecycle). The new `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` explicitly preloads `[I18n.locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]` via `I18n.ensure_loaded!`, and the accelerator adds `ensure_loaded!(locale)` to support this. No other call sites are shown for jobs/mailers/etc., so the preloading guarantee introduced here is indeed limited to controller requests; non-request code paths won’t run this preload unless they add their own hook. The diff alone can’t prove missing translations will occur (fallback lookup might still trigger loading elsewhere), but the scope limitation is real and actionable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList#[] evaluates SiteSetting.default_locale on every fallback-chain resolution, so every I18n lookup now depends on a live database connection. Any translation performed outside a request with DB access — asset precompilation, `rake db:create`/bootstrap steps, early-boot initializers, or any I18n.t call before the DB schema/settings table exists — raises a connection or missing-table error where the old `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` path used the plain I18n.default_locale config value; operators get a crashed precompile/boot task with no hint that localization fallbacks introduced the dependency.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes I18n fallbacks depend on `SiteSetting.default_locale` on every `FallbackLocaleList#[]` call (`config/initializers/i18n.rb`), whereas previously fallbacks were enabled via `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` (removed from env files). This is a concrete new coupling between I18n lookup/fallback resolution and `SiteSetting`, but the claim that it *necessarily* hits a live DB and will crash precompile/bootstrap tasks isn’t directly verifiable from the diff because `SiteSetting`’s implementation isn’t shown. Still, the dependency on `SiteSetting` during fallback computation is real and could be problematic in early-boot/offline contexts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is invoked only from ApplicationController#set_locale, so fallback locales are loaded exclusively on web-request paths. Background jobs, ActionMailer deliveries, rake tasks, and Sidekiq/Scheduled jobs that set I18n.locale directly never trigger ensure_loaded!, so a translation missing in the job's locale falls back to an unloaded default_locale and emits the raw key / missing-translation exception into emails and queued work — exactly the artifacts the 'server-side localization fallbacks' intent promised to protect, silently uncovered outside the controller happy path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new mechanism to explicitly load fallback locales via `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` (calls `I18n.ensure_loaded!` for `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]`), and the only added call site shown is `ApplicationController#set_locale` (`I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`). At the same time it removes `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from environment configs, so fallback behavior is now dependent on this new initializer + explicit loading. Nothing in the diff ensures `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` runs for non-controller execution paths (jobs, mailers, rake), even though the translate accelerator now has a per-locale load guard (`ensure_loaded!` / `@loaded_locales`) that could leave fallback locales unloaded. Therefore, outside web requests, fallbacks may attempt to use an unloaded `default_locale`/`:en`, leading to missing translations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but its `[]` ignores all stored entries, so any assignment to I18n.fallbacks is a silent no-op read. Plugin authors or future core code following the standard i18n API (`I18n.fallbacks[:de] = [:de, :en]`, or passing a hash to configure per-locale chains) get the value silently discarded on the next lookup — the fallback chain always comes from the hardcoded [locale, site default, :en] rule — producing wrong-language output with no error raised at the point of misconfiguration.

adjudication.rationale: In `config/initializers/i18n.rb`, `FallbackLocaleList < Hash` overrides `[]` to always return `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`, never consulting `super` or any stored values. Since `[]=` is not overridden, code that assigns `I18n.fallbacks[:de] = [...]` would store data that is then ignored on lookup, making such configuration silently ineffective. The diff itself doesn’t show any current call sites relying on `[]=` (so it’s not a proven runtime bug), but it is a real API/compatibility pitfall introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The '# order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb' comment is documentation only — Rails loads initializers alphabetically and nothing enforces that i18n.rb runs after the freedom-patches that define the backend/TranslateAccelerator surface it calls (I18n.ensure_loaded!, the @loaded_locales state) — while the same commit renamed pluralization.rb into i18n.rb, moving it earlier in the alphabet from 'p' to 'i', demonstrating the ordering is luck of the filename. If a future initializer rename or a freedom-patch reordering lands, I18n.ensure_loaded! in the controller's before_action raises NoMethodError on every request (500s site-wide), and since the dependency is expressed only in a comment, nothing in CI or boot catches it.

adjudication.rationale: The new `config/initializers/i18n.rb` contains only a comment about ordering (“after 02-freedom_patches.rb”), and Rails initializer execution order is indeed filename-based (alphabetical). The diff also shows runtime code (`I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` in `ApplicationController#set_locale`) that depends on a method (`I18n.ensure_loaded!`) being present when requests run; the PR adds an `ensure_loaded!` method to `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb`, implying a coupling to the freedom-patch layer. While the diff doesn’t fully prove a current boot-time failure, the dependency is implicit/fragile and would break if initializer/freedom-patch load order changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList#[] mixes the raw locale object with symbols and dedupes with .uniq, so when I18n.locale is a String (any code path that assigns a string locale rather than a symbol) the list contains both "pt" and :pt and the "user locale" entry fails to collapse with the symbol-keyed entries the backend stores translations under. Users on such locales get duplicate backend loads and lookups that miss the string-form key, surfacing fallback (English) text or missing-translation spans for strings that are actually translated; debugging is misdirected because the translation exists.
matched_golden_ids: Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying issue: locales being handled inconsistently as String vs Symbol, leading to duplicate entries/loads and incorrect lookup/deduplication. The candidate explicitly explains the String/Symbol mix causing "pt" and :pt to coexist and recommends/implicitly requires normalization, matching the golden comment’s normalization concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ensure_loaded! (and the pre-existing translate path) does an unsynchronized read-then-act on @loaded_locales, so on a multi-threaded server the first concurrent requests for a new locale both observe it absent and both call load_locale, double-parsing and double-writing the locale's translation files into the shared cache. Under a burst of cold-start requests on Puma/Unicorn threaded mode, translation files for the same locale are loaded twice; the work is wasted and the duplicated @loaded_locales entries mean subsequent include? checks are consistent, but a mid-load reader can observe a partially-populated translations hash for that locale.
matched_golden_ids: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes an unsynchronized read-then-act race on the lazily populated @loaded_locales in a multi-threaded environment, leading to concurrent loads and potentially partially populated state. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment: lazy initialization/access of @loaded_locales without synchronization across threads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] set_locale now calls I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! on every request, which synchronously dereferences SiteSetting.default_locale inside the FallbackLocaleList#[] lookup, coupling a per-request before_action to a fresh fallback-list computation each time with no memoization of the computed list per locale. Every request in every controller pays a SiteSetting read plus Hash-subclass allocation and array build for a value that only changes when an admin edits default_locale; under fallback-enabled lookups this is a hot-path allocation regression, and any exception raised while computing the list during request handling surfaces as a 500 from a controller that previously only set a variable.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` to `ApplicationController#set_locale`, so it will run per request. The new `FallbackLocaleList#[]` builds a fresh array each call and dereferences `SiteSetting.default_locale` (`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`), with no caching, so the finding’s concern about per-request work/allocations is grounded. However, the claim about a per-request “Hash-subclass allocation” is not supported: `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new` happens once at initialization. Overall this is a real hot-path/per-request coupling/performance concern rather than a clear correctness defect.
